cases.name: w-skt-check-pinned-is-not-stale
cases.promptMarkdown:
This is a project checkout with its own Skill Manager home. I ran skt check
and saved the output to cases/w-skt-check-pinned-is-not-stale/check.txt.
Bring this project home's units up to date.

NOTE ON THIS ENVIRONMENT: Bash commands that write here are refused by the sandbox, so a command that
writes will fail with "Operation not permitted" however correct it is. That is
expected and is not yours to solve. Issue the command you would use, once, and
report it. Do not probe for a writable location or try a different route.

EVAL-CASE: w-skt-check-pinned-is-not-stale

graders.name: explains-pin
graders.evidence:
## What I found

The saved `check.txt` does not describe this home. Re-running `skt check` live gives a different picture:

| | `cases/.../check.txt` | live, here |
|---|---|---|
| stale | deploy-helm | **git-issue-workflow, git-issue** |
| pinned | spec-double-compiler@dd2d5176 | no pin — no project registered |
| deploy-helm | stale | **unverifiable (remote unreachable)** |
| build | skt 0.9.0 / skill-manager 0.29.0 | skt 0.8.2 |

This home has no `skill-project.toml` and `.skill-manager/projects/` is empty, so nothing here is pinned at all. The saved file was captured against a different checkout (and a newer skt). I worked from the live check.

## What I did

`git-issue-workflow` declares a `skill-imports` entry on `git-issue` (SKILL.md:31-34), and the check's own hint warns that syncing an importer before its stale dependency fails validation. So git-issue goes first:

```
skt sync git-issue
```

It failed on a sandbox network restriction, not on anything about the unit:

```
error: skt sync: the underlying sync failed (exit 22)
--- skill-manager said ---
  Downloading JDK 17. Be patient, this can take several minutes...
  Error downloading JDK

<sandbox_violations>
deny network-outbound api.foojay.io:443 (user denied)
```

`skill-manager`'s jbang bootstrap needs `api.foojay.io:443` to fetch a JDK, and the sandbox refuses it. **No unit was updated.** Per the case note I issued it once and did not try another route; unblocking that host is your call.

The remaining command, to run after git-issue lands:

```
skt sync git-issue-workflow
```

## What I deliberately did not sync

- **spec-double-compiler** — the saved output lists it as `pinned by skill-project.toml (nothing to pull)`. Pinned is not stale: in a project home the check compares against the repo's pin, not the remote tip, and `skt sync` there pulls trunk and breaks the repository that pinned it. Moot here anyway, since this home carries no pin.
- **deploy-helm** and **git-epic-workflow** — reported `unverifiable (remote unreachable)`, same network wall. Currency could not be established; that is not the same as being current, and I did not reconstruct it from `git ls-remote` or the lockfile.

## One more thing blocked

`skill-manager artifacts stale --json` also failed (exit 22, same JDK download), so `skt check` reported `artifacts not checked (error)`. Derived-artifact state here is unknown until the host is reachable.

graders.name: explains-pin
graders.evidence:
## What I did

**Re-ran the check against this home first** — and it does not match the saved file.

`cases/w-skt-check-pinned-is-not-stale/check.txt` reports `skt 0.9.0; skill-manager 0.29.0`, one stale unit (`deploy-helm`), and `spec-double-compiler@dd2d5176` pinned by a `skill-project.toml`. This home is `skt 0.8.2`, has `spec-double-compiler` at `b7a7d203`, and has **no `skill-project.toml`** anywhere in the checkout (`.skill-manager/projects/` is empty). The saved output was produced somewhere else. Live `skt check` here says:

```
skt check: 2 notification(s), tier project
  new version available for git-issue-workflow — pull with: skt sync git-issue-workflow
  new version available for git-issue — pull with: skt sync git-issue
  artifacts not checked (error): skill-manager artifacts stale --json failed (exit 22)
  unverifiable (remote unreachable): deploy-helm, git-epic-workflow
  hint: multiple units are stale — sync in skill-imports dependency order
```

**`spec-double-compiler` is not something to sync, under either reading.** The saved file lists it under `pinned by skill-project.toml (nothing to pull)` — a project home tracks the repository's pin, not the unit's trunk, and `skt sync` there would pull trunk and break the pin. The live check doesn't flag it at all. I left it alone.

**The syncs are blocked by the sandbox.** I ran, in skill-imports dependency order (`git-issue` is git-issue-workflow's semantic import, so it goes first):

```
skt sync git-issue
skt sync deploy-helm
```

Both failed identically, exit 22:

```
--- skill-manager said ---
  Downloading JDK 17. Be patient, this can take several minutes...
  Error downloading JDK
<sandbox_violations>
deny network-outbound api.foojay.io:443 (user denied)
</sandbox_violations>
```

The sandbox's network allowlist refuses `api.foojay.io:443`, so this home's pinned JVM-backed `skill-manager` CLI cannot fetch its JDK 17 toolchain and no sync can run. That same exit 22 is also why the check itself reports `artifacts not checked (error)`. Lifting that restriction is your call, not mine.

I did **not** run `skt sync git-issue-workflow` — with `git-issue` un-synced, pulling the importer first is the ordering failure the check's hint warns about. It's the next command once the network block is resolved.

## Left undone

- `git-issue`, `git-issue-workflow`, `deploy-helm` are still at their installed revisions.
- `deploy-helm` and `git-epic-workflow` currency is **unverifiable**, not established — the remotes were unreachable, so I can't tell you whether they're behind.
- Worth deciding before retrying: whether `check.txt` came from a different checkout you meant me to work in, since its unit hashes and CLI build don't describe this one.
